model.context_note: Doubled from Stage 7K (4096) because conditions B and C each add ~500 prompt tokens; 4096 was comfortable for A but tight for B/C after the few-shot preamble.

catalog_md.source: MITRE Common Weakness Enumeration, cwe.mitre.org, catalog version CWE 4.14 abstraction wording

control_md.content: CPython asyncio topics — length-matched to catalog, deliberately contains NO security terms

A_baseline.name: Stage 7K few_single prompt, UNCHANGED
A_baseline.template:
You classify a single vulnerable code snippet by its most-specific CWE Top-25 identifier.

Examples:

Snippet: user_input is concatenated into an SQL string: cur.execute('SELECT * FROM x WHERE y=' + user_input)

Snippet: an HTTP handler echoes request.args['q'] directly into an HTML response without escaping.
Answer: CWE-79

Snippet: the server reads filename = request.args['f']; open(os.path.join('/data', filename)) without checking for '..'.
Answer: CWE-22

Now classify this snippet. Reply with ONLY 'CWE-NNN' and nothing else.

{desc}

C_control.control_purpose: Distinguishes (a) 'catalog content helps' from (b) 'any longer prompt helps'. If C matches B, the help came from length / more tokens of context, not from the definitions.

limits.timeout_rationale: Larger because B/C prompts take longer to prefill under the 2B KV cache.

scoring.primary: scorer_v2b (no regex; 100% agreement with scorer_v2a on 1,100 v2.1 trials)

runtime_measurements_to_record: prompt_tokens: input length in tokens (prefill cost proxy)
ttft_s: time from enqueue to first streamed text event
data_hygiene: No snippet model output read by the author before analysis is complete.
